land.text: the former British Somaliland, which 'obtained independence as the State of Somaliland' on 26 June 1960 and 'united as planned to form the Somali Republic' on 1 July 1960

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Federal Republic of Somalia row (1960-2024) still draws the north as Somali land; that dossier should record the loss in 1991.

correction.text: the former British protectorate of Somaliland, 'claimed territory has an area of 176,120 square kilometres'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; its Federal Republic of Somalia row still includes the north). 'Between 27 April and 15 May 1991, a conference in Burao saw the local administration declare the northwestern Somali territories independent'; infobox 'Declaration of independence: 18 May 1991'. The claimed area is 176,120 km2 (text) or 177,125 km2 (infobox); the Natural Earth Somaliland polygon resolves to about 203,000 km2 in the gazetteer (ratio 1.15), because it runs east over Sool and eastern Sanaag, which Puntland and later SSC-Khatumo dispute. Somaliland did not control all of this: the Sool-Sanaag zone is a dispute (contest events), not a settled hold.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Following the Las Anod conflict that began in 2022, Somaliland lost control of a significant portion of its eastern territory'; SSC-Khatumo 'includes parts of the Sool, Sanaag and Togdheer regions' and 'effectively took over those regions, securing most of their claimed area'. The lost zone is drawn as a 120 km circle round Las Anod (about 45,000 km2), the researcher's reading: the pages opened give no boundary. 'It is currently in control of the vast majority of the former State of Somaliland.'

ledger.note: 1991 (18 May): the Somaliland north declares independence from Somalia. Infobox 'Declaration of independence: 18 May 1991'; a conference at Burao between 27 April and 15 May 1991 saw the local administration declare 'the northwestern Somali territories independent'. Hargeisa is the capital.

ledger.note: 2007 (October): Somaliland takes Las Anod. 'In October 2007, Somaliland troops took control of the town' of Las Anod. The dispute over eastern Sanaag and parts of Sool with Puntland goes on; Khatumo State was declared on 12 January 2012 (Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page).

region.text: Las Anod and the Dhulbahante lands round it inside Somaliland's claimed territory (Sool and the neighbouring Togdheer and Sanaag cells), not the Nugaal and Mudug cells of Puntland the 120 km disc also reached: Las Anod and the Dhulbahante lands round it, the 'parts of the Sool, Sanaag and Togdheer regions' held by SSC-Khatumo

ledger.note: 2007 (October): Las Anod is Somaliland's. 'In October 2007, Somaliland troops took control of the town' of Las Anod. The page does not name who held it before; Puntland is the disputing party on the Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page. [fx-44, R150: the Las Anod disc of 120 km (215 cells) reaches 22 cells of Puntland's Nugaal (19) and Mudug (3), which the gain handed to Somaliland, and 42 cells of Ethiopia; it is intersected with the Somaliland claim (the keyframe country, 151 of the disc's cells). Las Anod page (opened 2026-11-03): 'Somaliland forces captured the city in the Battle of Las Anod in 2007, ousting Puntland forces'; the page does not date or draw the frontline afterwards, so the extent beyond the town is the claim's, confidence 3 -> 2.]

ledger.note: 2023: the Las Anod conflict opens. Mass protests 'from December into January 2023'; 'the conflict erupted in early 2023'; on 6 February 2023 'the Dhulbahante clan elders declared their intent to form a state government named SSC-Khatumo within Somalia'. By 25 August 2023 SSC forces had 'overrun two strongholds of the Somaliland National Army in Maraaga and Goja'adde'.

region.text: Las Anod and the Dhulbahante lands round it, the 'parts of the Sool, Sanaag and Togdheer regions' held by SSC-Khatumo

ledger.note: 2023: Somaliland loses Las Anod and the east. 'Somaliland lost control of a significant portion of its eastern territory' (Somaliland page); 'the retreat of the Somaliland troops paved the way for the return of the supreme Garad' (Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page); the Federal Government recognised SSC-Khatumo as an interim administration on 19 October 2023 and renamed it the North Eastern State of Somalia on 30 July 2025. The pages give no date for the withdrawal.

wars.outcome: SSC-Khatumo took Las Anod and most of its claimed area from Somaliland in 2023; 'a military stalemate presently holds' with the front 'about 100km away from the city of Las Anod' as of August 2024.
wars.note: The conflict article was not opened. Protests began in December 2022; the front line was first about 170 km from Las Anod and later shifted to western Sool between Oog and Guumays (Sool, Sanaag and Cayn page).

notes:
Cliopatria has no Somaliland row; its Federal Republic of Somalia row (1960-2024) still draws the north, so the Somalia dossier needs a loss event in 1991 (and the same for the Puntland and SSC-Khatumo zones). Somaliland is unrecognised: the Somaliland page says it is 'recognised by one UN member state' (Israel, 26 December 2025) and that an Ethiopia memorandum of 1 January 2024 would give Ethiopia a lease of Berbera; none of this moves a border.
Not settled: the extent of Somaliland's actual hold on Sool and eastern Sanaag before 2007 (the pages give no map, and Natural Earth draws the whole claim); Erigavo and Buhoodle events (the Somaliland page only lists them as the Sanaag capital and a Togdheer district); the date of the withdrawal from Las Anod (the pages say 'early 2023'); the 2012-2017 Khatumo State (declared by about 2,300 Dhulbahante representatives on 12 January 2012, 'practically ceased to function' by 2015) and the Aynabo agreement of October 2017. The SNM war of 1988-1991 (offensive on Hargeisa and Burao in May 1988) precedes the state and is not a war entry. The 2023 contest is still open at 2024 ('a military stalemate presently holds').
Counterparts needing dossiers: puntland (1998-2024), ssc-khatumo (2023-2024; renamed North Eastern State of Somalia on 30 July 2025). Gazetteer: no new names (the country Somaliland and the places Laascaanood and Ceerigaabo exist).
